q-216934.name: Question 1
q-216934.problem:
Consider the equations of the following lines.

I. $3y=5$

II. $-x+7y=0$

III. $5x-3y=6$

Which of these lines is written in standard form?
q-216934.worked_solution:
The *standard form* equation of a line is 

$$
ax+by=c,
$$

where

- $a,b,$ and $c$ are all integers,

- $a\ge 0,$ and

- $a,b,$ and $c$ have no common factors greater than $1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our equations.

- Equation I is in standard form. Indeed, the variables are on the left-hand side, while the constant term is on the right-hand side:

$$
{{3y}_{⏟}}_{\text{variables}}\,={{5}_{⏟}}_{\text{constant}}
$$

 
All coefficients are integers (namely, $3$ and $5$) and don't have common factors greater than $1.$ Also, the coefficient of $x$ is non-negative ($0$).

- Equation II is *not* in standard form because the coefficient of $x$ is negative ($-1$).

- Equation III is in standard form. Indeed, the variables are on the left-hand side, while the constant term is on the right-hand side:

$$
{{5x-3y}_{⏟}}_{\text{variables}}\,={{6}_{⏟}}_{\text{constant}}
$$

 
All coefficients are integers (namely, $5,$ $-3,$ and $6$) and don't have common factors greater than $1.$ Also, the coefficient of $x$ is positive ($5$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

q-109609.name: Question 4
q-109609.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-7x-4 \\ 7x+y & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is $7x+y=-4.$

q-214594.name: Question 5
q-214594.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

$$
-\frac{2}{5}x+y=-3
$$

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}x+y & =-3 \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{2}{5}x+y) & =(-1)\cdot (-3) \\ \frac{2}{5}x-y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}x-y & =3 \\ 5\cdot (\frac{2}{5}x-y) & =5\cdot (3) \\ 2x-5y & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is 

$$
2x-5y=15.
$$

Our goal is to write the equation in the form ax+by=c, where a,b, and c are integers with no common factors and a≥0.

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side. This gives

−25x+y=−3

Now, we multiply both sides of the equation by −1:

−25x+y=−3(−1)⋅(−25x+y)=(−1)⋅(−3)25x−y=3

Finally, we multiply both sides of the equation by 5:

25x−y=35⋅(25x−y)=5⋅(3)2x−5y=15

Now, a,b, and c are integers with no common factors, and a≥0. So we are done!

The standard form of the line is 2x−5y=15.

q-13339.name: Question 7
q-13339.worked_solution:
Our goal is to write the equation in the form $ax+by=c,$ where $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors and $a\ge 0.$

We begin by moving all of the variables to the left-hand side and all of the constants to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y+3x+3 & =0 \\ 3x+3y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now the equation is in the form $ax+by=c.$ However, $a,b,$ and $c$ have a common factor of $3.$ So, we divide by $3$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+3y & =-3 \\ \frac{3x+3y}{3} & =\frac{-3}{3} \\ x+y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $a,b,$ and $c$ are integers with no common factors, and $a\ge 0.$ So we are done!

The standard form of the line is $x+y=-1.$

q-109627.name: Question 8
q-109627.problem: What is the equation of the line that passes through the points $(-5,5)$ and $(-1,6)$, expressed in standard form?
q-109627.worked_solution:
First, we will construct the point-slope form of the line. Then, we will simplify it into standard form.

To construct the point-slope form of the line, we need a point and a slope. We already have two points, so we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{6-5}{-1-(-5)}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use this slope along with one of the points to write the point-slope form equation of the line. It doesn't matter which point we choose, but let's choose $(-5,5).$ The point-slope equation is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5 & =\frac{1}{4}(x-(-5)) \\ y-5 & =\frac{1}{4}(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

To simplify the point-slope formula into standard form, we first multiply by $4$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-5 & =\frac{1}{4}(x+5) \\ 4\cdot (y-5) & =4\cdot \frac{1}{4}(x+5) \\ 4y-20 & =x+5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we move the variables to the left side and the constant to the right side:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-20 & =x+5 \\ 4y & =x+25 \\ -x+4y & =25\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply by $-1$ to make the $x$-coefficient positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+4y & =25 \\ (-1)\cdot (-x+4y) & =(-1)\cdot 25 \\ x-4y & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

So, the standard form of the equation is $x-4y=-25.$

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{4-(-2)}{-1-(-3)}=\frac{6}{2}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use this slope along with one of the points to write the point-slope form equation of the line. It doesn't matter which point we choose, but let's choose $(-1,4).$ The point-slope equation is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =3(x-(-1)) \\ y-4 & =3(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we simplify the point-slope formula into standard form, moving the variables to the left side and the constant to the right side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4 & =3(x+1) \\ y-4 & =3x+3 \\ y & =3x+7 \\ -3x+y & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply by $-1$ to make the $x$-coefficient positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+y & =7 \\ (-1)\cdot (-3x+y) & =(-1)\cdot 7 \\ 3x-y & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the standard form of the equation is 

$$
3x-y=-7.
$$
